questions.question: Can anything launch a second reviewer?
questions.answer: No path found. `review_candidate` launches only when `automatic-review.json` is absent (automatic.py:234) AND `review-worktree` is absent (:257-258); the receipt is written before the helper runs (:297, :374). `run_reviewer` independently refuses when `review.interactive.json` exists (interactive.py:200) or a session with the launch name exists (:207-208). The `retry`/`reconcile` CLI actions re-enter the node only through `review_candidate`, which returns or raises on any existing receipt (:236-255); `reconcile` never reaches the reviewer (pipeline.py:686-694). Tests assert one launch across interrupt, failure and rejection paths (test_automatic.py:568, 646, 651, 684, 708, 741).

questions.question: Can an unbound completion file be accepted?
questions.answer: No. `read_review_completion` requires schema validity plus exact `run_id`, `node_id=="review"`, `launch_token` equal to the receipt's fresh uuid4, `bundle_sha256` equal to the recomputed bundle digest, and `candidate_commit` (automatic.py:181-201); `_accept_native` then re-checks session identity, independence from worker UUIDs, worktree cleanliness at the candidate, and bundle/diff hashes (:332-339). Symlinks and >256 KiB files are refused (:187-188); the reviewer has no Bash to create either. Nothing downstream re-reads `review.completion.json` (grep of export_state/server/src).

questions.question: Can a live reviewer session be lost?
questions.answer: Ctrl-C at any point after `claude --bg` was issued, and any termination while waiting, are recoverable (receipt `running`, langgraph records no error, resume re-enters `_accept_native`). Two fail-closed traps remain, both P2 above: a non-KeyboardInterrupt termination inside the launch window leaves `launching`, which resume refuses despite the binding handle being on disk; and a reviewer session that exits (e.g. closed by the operator in its pane) after writing a valid file but before acceptance/stop blocks the run permanently. Neither relaunches or accepts anything wrongly; both require a new run.

decisions: `review.attempt` is hard-coded to 1 (workflow/export_state.py:88): one reviewer per run by design; a run can never expose a second attempt.

`transport` is inferred from file existence, not from the receipt's `transport` field (workflow/export_state.py:62-68): `automatic-review.json` at `launching`/`needs_reconciliation`/`blocked` with no `review.interactive.json` counts as `print` for legacy plans, even though native receipts record `transport: native` (workflow/automatic.py:295).

`reviewed_at` fallback takes the LAST review-node event of any status (workflow/export_state.py:79-80). For a blocked native review there is no `accepted_at` (`_decide` raises before `receipt.update`, workflow/automatic.py:284-288) and the last event is the reviewer `stopped` event (workflow/pipeline.py:221), so `reviewed_at` is the stop time, not the verdict time.
`inputs.mode` is derived from the presence of `plan.automatic` (workflow/export_state.py:143), never from `plan.mode`, which prepare always sets to `interactive` (workflow/pipeline.py:618).

`launch` projection drops `worktree`, `plan_digest`, `base_commit`, `attempt` and `error` from `<node>.interactive.json` (workflow/export_state.py:93-101): a `needs_reconciliation` receipt exports its status without its reason; absolute worktree paths never reach the export.

`native_started_at` is exported only when the receipt value is exactly `int` (workflow/export_state.py:100); any other type from `claude agents --json` `startedAt` (interactive.py:120) is silently null. The real type was not verified offline.

`stop.confirmed_at` is the stop file's mtime (workflow/export_state.py:121), relying on `stop_session` rewriting the intent file at confirmation (workflow/pipeline.py:208-209); it is not a recorded timestamp.
`max_verification_attempts` defaults to 3 when absent (workflow/export_state.py:151), matching the pipeline's own default (workflow/pipeline.py:277).

`inputs` can only be null via `ExportRuntime` without `policy.json` (workflow/pipeline.py:428-431); a live `Pipeline` always has a policy (workflow/pipeline.py:119), and the export runs at `prepare` (workflow/pipeline.py:625) so `inputs` exists from the start with all receipts null.
`hashlib.file_digest` (workflow/export_state.py:85) requires Python ≥ 3.11; the packet loop still uses `sha256(read_bytes())` (:170). The project venv is 3.12.3.
`zulu()` only rewrites `+00:00` (workflow/export_state.py:38-40); receipts are always written with `timezone.utc` (interactive.py:165,212) so this suffices.

Legacy automatic plans (no `reviewer_transport`) resolve to `native` at runtime (workflow/automatic.py:58-60) and the export reports what the receipts recorded instead (workflow/export_state.py:148); these two views are intentionally different.

`transport: manual` can only occur for non-automatic plans: the `review --review-file` CLI requires a pending `independent_review` interrupt (workflow/pipeline.py:673-675), which only manual plans raise (workflow/pipeline.py:468-473).

questions.question: When is `review` null, and when is each of its fields null?
questions.answer: `review` is null unless `review.json` exists and parses (workflow/export_state.py:72-74). `diff` is null when `review.diff` is absent or a symlink (:81-85). `findings[].worker`/`requirement` are null when the persisted review lacks them, i.e. any review recorded before this change (:86-87). `reviewed_at` is never null: receipt `accepted_at` → last review-node event → `review.json` mtime (:77-80). `transport` is never null: native/print/manual (:76).

questions.question: When is `inputs` null, and when are its nested parts null?
questions.answer: `inputs` is null only when there is no policy (no `runtime.policy` and no `policy.json`, :171,:177), which can only happen via `ExportRuntime`. `automatic` is null for manual plans (:144); `automatic.reviewer_transport` is null only for a legacy plan with neither `review.interactive.json` nor `automatic-review.json` (:148, :62-68). Per worker: `prompt` null when `<node>.prompt.txt` is missing/symlink (:128); `launch` null when `<node>.interactive.json` is absent/invalid or lacks string `launch_requested_at`/`launch_token`/`status` or int `launcher_invocations` (:93-96); `completion` null unless status is completed|blocked with non-empty summary and a list of non-empty strings (:104-107); `handoff` null on the same summary/assumptions rule (:111-113); `stop` null unless the file has a boolean `stopped`, and `stop.confirmed_at` null when `stopped` is false (:117-121). `source_branch` and `failure_drill` pass through as null when absent (:143,:152).

risks.evidence: Both tab buttons always set `aria-controls="run-panel-<id>"`, but only the selected panel is rendered (`tab === 'assignment' ? <AssignmentPanel …/> : <div role="tabpanel" id="run-panel-run">`), so the inactive tab references an id that is not in the DOM.

risks.evidence: `tab` only changes in `setTab` calls from click/keyboard, `navigateToNode` and `openRequirement`; a route change that arrives via props (browser Back/Forward, or a pasted `/nodes/<id>` URL after the tab was switched) leaves `tab === 'assignment'`, so the Assignment panel stays on screen while the URL names a node.

risks.evidence: The comment says the pending quote is 'dropped once applied or when leaving it', but the only clearing path is `onHighlightApplied` from `TaskPanel`'s mount effect, and `TaskPanel` mounts only when `worker !== null` (inputs ready and matched). Leaving the node merely masks it (`pendingHighlight.nodeId === selectedNodeId`). If the reader clicks a finding link while inputs are still loading or errored and moves on, the stale quote is applied (Source view forced, mark scrolled) the next time that node is opened from the list.
risks.why: A later, unrelated visit to the worker node behaves as if a finding had just been followed; add a reset on `selectedNodeId` change or clear in NodeDetail when the panel cannot mount.

risks.evidence: `executed` is null for every non-ready state; the message distinguishes only `loading` from everything else, so a result whose fetch failed (`result.status === 'error'`) is captioned 'No published result to compare against.' even though `result_uri` exists and the Result section below shows an ErrorPanel.
risks.why: Says a result does not exist when it does; 'could not be loaded' would be accurate.

risks.evidence: `handoffDiffers` is true when `completion === null && handoff !== null`, and the section then prints 'The accepted handoff differs from what the worker reported.' while the completion section just above says 'No completion signal recorded.'
risks.why: The sentence asserts a difference from a report that does not exist; wording should cover the no-completion case.

risks.evidence: When the inputs request fails (anything but INPUTS_NOT_FOUND), the header renders an `ErrorPanel` (role=alert with Retry) and a selected worker node renders a second identical one for the same resource.
